newsitem.title: UK: UK tobacco industry raps budget duty increase.
newsitem.headline: UK tobacco industry raps budget duty increase.

text.p: Britain's tobacco industry said it was disappointed on Wednesday by British Chancellor Gordon Brown's decision to implement a sharp increase in duty on cigarettes.
"In the normal course of events the price of a packet of 20 cigarettes would have risen by over 14p, under my proposals the price of a packet will rise on December 1 by 19p," said Brown.
Clive Inston, head of corporate affairs at Imperial, said: "We are not surprised but disappointed. Our major concern is that this is just going to fund the bootlegging trade."
He calculated that the increase would mean a pack of 20 premium brand cigarettes in Britain would now cost 3.31 pence against the equivalent 1.90 pence in France.
In a statement The Tobacco Manufacturers Association also expressed disappointment with the Chancellor's decision.

The Chancellor announced a freezing of duty on hand rolling tobacco, which currently costs about 7.57 stg per 50 gram pouch, and a 10p rise in duty on a 50 gram pack of pipe tobacco and 10p on a pack of five cigars.
Amanda Sandford of ASH, Action on Smoking and Health, said the increase would lead to a reduction in smoking of 2.2 billion cigarettes a year which in the long run will save 3,500 lives a year.

Imperial Tobacco Group Plc shares were 6p lower at 380p and Gallaher Group Plc were down 5-1/2p at 273p at the close. Gallaher makes Benson & Hedges, Silk Cut and Old Holborn rolling tobacco. Imperial owns the John Player Special and Embassy brands.
Former Chancellor Kenneth Clarke raised tax on a packet of 20 cigarettes by 15 pence, by seven pence on a pack of small cigars and eight pence on a packet of pipe tobacco.
He said this was in line with a commitment to raise tobacco duty by more than the rate of inflation each year.
